senses.definition: The hard frame of bones that supports a person or animal.
senses.example: An X-ray can show part of your skeleton.

senses.definition: A tough, bendy body material found in places such as your ears and joints.
senses.example: Cartilage covers the ends of the bones at many joints.

senses.definition: Soft tissue inside certain bones. One kind makes new blood cells.
senses.example: The red bone marrow in some bones makes blood cells.

senses.definition: A place where bones meet.
senses.example: Your elbow is a joint that lets your arm bend.

senses.definition: A strong band of body tissue that helps join bones and guide motion at a joint.
senses.example: A ligament helps keep the bones of the knee steady.

senses.definition: One of the bones that form the spine.
senses.example: Each vertebra helps protect the spinal cord.

senses.definition: The group of bones that shapes the head and surrounds the brain.
senses.example: The skull protects the brain.

senses.definition: Curved bones and nearby cartilage that surround the chest and protect parts inside it.
senses.example: My rib cage moves when I take a deep breath.

senses.definition: A cell in the blood that carries oxygen to the body.
senses.example: A red blood cell changes shape to pass through a narrow tube.

senses.definition: A cell that helps protect the body and respond to things such as germs.
senses.example: Different white blood cells do different protection jobs.

senses.definition: The main liquid part of your blood, in which cells and other things travel.
senses.example: Water and dissolved nutrients are carried in plasma.

senses.definition: A tiny piece of a cell that travels in blood and helps stop bleeding.
senses.example: Platelets collect at the spot where a vessel is damaged.

senses.definition: A material in red blood cells that can pick up oxygen and let it go again.
senses.example: Hemoglobin gives red blood cells their color.

senses.definition: A lump that forms when pieces and materials in blood stick together.
senses.example: A clot may close a small cut.

senses.definition: A tube inside an animal that carries blood.
senses.example: Blood moving through a blood vessel brings supplies to cells.

senses.definition: A tube that carries blood away from the heart.
senses.example: Blood leaves the heart in an artery.

senses.definition: A tube that carries blood back toward the heart.
senses.example: A vein in my leg brings blood toward my heart.

senses.definition: A tiny tube where materials can pass between blood and nearby tissue.
senses.example: The red blood cell passes through a narrow capillary.

senses.definition: A body part made of tissues that work together to do one or more jobs.
senses.example: The heart is an organ that pumps blood.

senses.definition: The thin, living cover on the outside of the body.
senses.example: Skin lets me feel the bumps on this leaf.

senses.definition: A tough material your body makes for parts such as hair, nails, and the outer layer of skin.
senses.example: Your fingernails contain keratin.

senses.definition: A tiny pocket in the body, such as the kind in skin where a hair begins.
senses.example: Each hair starts to grow inside a follicle.

senses.definition: An organ that sorts and changes some things brought by the blood and makes a liquid that helps digest fats.
senses.example: The liver makes bile which can reach the small intestine.

senses.definition: A liquid made by the liver that helps the body digest fats.
senses.example: Bile helps spread fat into small droplets.

senses.definition: A small pouch under the liver that stores some bile.
senses.example: During digestion, the gallbladder releases bile into a tube.

senses.definition: An organ behind the stomach that makes helpers for digestion and sends messages such as insulin into the blood.
senses.example: The pancreas helps the small intestine break food down.

senses.definition: A tiny biological helper that speeds up a change, such as breaking food into smaller pieces.
senses.example: An enzyme in saliva starts breaking down some starch from bread.

senses.definition: A chemical message made in your body that changes what some cells do.
senses.example: A hormone can tell cells to let sugar in from the blood.

senses.definition: A gland near the front of the neck that makes messages that help set how fast your body uses energy.
senses.example: The thyroid releases hormones into the blood.

senses.definition: A small gland below the brain that makes and releases messages used by other parts of the body.
senses.example: One message from the pituitary gland reaches the thyroid.

senses.definition: The light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye.
senses.example: Light lands on the retina and some of its cells send signals.

senses.definition: The round opening that lets light into an eye.
senses.example: My pupil becomes smaller in bright light.

senses.definition: The colored ring in an eye that changes the size of the opening in its center.
senses.example: Her iris is brown.

senses.definition: The bundle of nerve fibers that carries signals from an eye to the brain.
senses.example: Signals about the picture leave the eye through the optic nerve.

senses.definition: A little passage that takes tears from near an eye toward the nose.
senses.example: Tears can drain through a tear duct.

senses.definition: The thin coat of tears that covers the front of an open eye.
senses.example: Blinking spreads the tear film.

senses.definition: A small group of cells that helps you sense tastes.
senses.example: A taste bud can help send a message when sugar touches your tongue.

senses.definition: A part of a cell or a nerve that notices a change and helps the body respond to it.
senses.example: A receptor can sense a light touch.

senses.definition: The part of the ear farthest from the outside that contains organs for hearing and balance.
senses.example: The inner ear sends clues about head movement to the brain.

senses.definition: A type of material that includes sugars, starches, and many kinds of fiber.
senses.example: Oatmeal contains more than one kind of carbohydrate.

senses.definition: A long chain of sugar units found in foods such as rice, flour, or potatoes.
senses.example: Starch in the potato can be broken into smaller sugars.

senses.definition: A material built from small parts called amino acids. Different proteins have different jobs in living things.
senses.example: One protein in my blood carries oxygen.

senses.definition: One of the small pieces a living body can join together to make a protein.
senses.example: A long chain can contain many copies of the same amino acid.

senses.definition: Parts of plant food that your own digestive juices break down only a little or not at all.
senses.example: An apple can provide dietary fiber.

senses.definition: A grain used with all of its main parts, including the outside and the part that can grow.
senses.example: Whole grain can still be whole when it is ground into flour.

senses.definition: A plant in the pea family or a food seed from such a plant.
senses.example: A lentil is a legume you can cook.

senses.definition: A substance from food or another source that your body needs in small quantities for its usual work.
senses.example: Different vegetables can supply different vitamins.

senses.definition: An element that is part of strong bones and teeth and helps nerves and muscles do their jobs.
senses.example: The nutrition label shows that the yogurt provides calcium.

senses.definition: An element that can be a metal and is also needed in tiny forms by the body to help carry oxygen.
senses.example: The beans in my lunch provide some iron.

senses.definition: How well the body has enough water to do its jobs.
senses.example: Drinking water as needed helps with hydration.

senses.definition: Information on packaged food about the amount of energy and certain nutrients it contains.
senses.example: I read the nutrition label to find out how much fiber is listed.

senses.definition: The stated amount of food or drink used to work out the numbers on a food label.
senses.example: The serving size printed on the label is half a cup.

senses.definition: The hard outer coat on the part of a tooth above the gums.
senses.example: Enamel protects a tooth when I chew.

senses.definition: A hollow space or, in a tooth, a hole caused by decay.
senses.example: A dentist can check for a cavity.

senses.definition: The long material carrying inherited information that many cells keep and use.
senses.example: The cell holds much of its DNA in a nucleus.

senses.definition: A thin layer around a cell that helps control what goes in and out.
senses.example: The cell membrane separates the watery inside from its surroundings.

senses.definition: A central part of many cells that holds most of their DNA.
senses.example: Chromosomes fit inside the nucleus.

senses.definition: A long piece of DNA and the proteins that help it fit inside a cell.
senses.example: A body cell usually has more than one chromosome.

senses.definition: A stretch of DNA whose information a cell can use for a particular job.
senses.example: One gene can tell a cell how to make a protein.

senses.definition: All the inherited information in a living thing.
senses.example: A plant’s genome contains directions for lots of different jobs.

senses.definition: One of the versions of DNA that can occur at a particular place.
senses.example: Two siblings may inherit a different allele at the same place in their DNA.

senses.definition: A feature of a living thing that can be noticed or measured.
senses.example: The color of a flower is a trait.

senses.definition: To get a feature or piece of genetic information from biological parents.
senses.example: Children inherit different mixes of DNA.

senses.definition: The distance from the bottom of something to its top, or how tall a person or object is.
senses.example: We measured the height of the plant from the soil to its top leaf.

senses.definition: A way a cell sorts copies of its chromosomes into two groups before it splits into two cells.
senses.example: Cells use mitosis as fresh skin grows.

senses.definition: One of two babies who began from the same fertilized egg and usually have very similar DNA.
senses.example: An identical twin can have likes and interests that differ from the other twin’s.

senses.definition: Two pieces that fit together as one rung on the ladder shape of DNA.
senses.example: Each base pair connects the two sides of DNA.

senses.definition: A small cell part that helps make energy from food available for the cell to use.
senses.example: A working muscle cell uses the energy its mitochondria help supply.

senses.definition: The organ inside your head that takes in signals and helps control the body.
senses.example: Your brain helps you remember what you learned yesterday.

senses.definition: The physical parts of a computer or other device that you could touch.
senses.example: The screen is part of the tablet’s hardware.

senses.definition: A chip or group of parts that follows instructions to do the work of a computer.
senses.example: The processor can quickly work out how to move the shapes on the screen.

senses.definition: The programs and other instructions a computer uses to do its work.
senses.example: Drawing software can turn my finger movements into a colored line.

senses.definition: A group of instructions a computer can follow.
senses.example: A program adds up how many points I earned.

senses.definition: Fast working memory that holds information a computer is using right now.
senses.example: When you restart, the computer can put the apps it needs back into RAM.

senses.definition: A part or place that keeps information for the computer to use later.
senses.example: The picture was saved in storage and still appeared after I restarted.

senses.definition: A collection of programs that helps apps and physical computer parts work together.
senses.example: The operating system tells different apps how to use the speaker.

senses.definition: A named group of information kept on a computer.
senses.example: I saved my picture as a file.

senses.definition: A named place that holds files or other folders on a computer.
senses.example: I put both drawings in a folder called Art.

senses.definition: A short ending after a dot in a filename, often used to show the type of file.
senses.example: The file extension .jpg often shows that a file holds a picture.

senses.definition: One of the tiny color points in a digital picture or display.
senses.example: A pixel in the sky part of the picture can be blue.

senses.definition: The amount of picture detail a grid can store, often described by how many pixels it has across and down.
senses.example: The image resolution is 300 pixels across and 200 pixels tall.

senses.definition: A way of describing colors by how much red, green, and blue light they use.
senses.example: A screen can combine RGB light to show yellow.

senses.definition: A saved picture described as shapes and lines that can be drawn again at different sizes.
senses.example: The vector image of a circle stayed smooth when we made it bigger.

senses.definition: A shared set of numbers that stand for text characters people use around the world.
senses.example: Unicode helps different phones agree on which letter to show.

senses.definition: A small part or measurement taken from something larger.
senses.example: A microphone recording can hold many sound samples from each second.

senses.definition: A way to store or send information in less space than it took before.
senses.example: Compression made my photo file smaller.

senses.definition: A collection of devices linked so they can share information.
senses.example: Our classroom computers can connect to a network and share a printer.

senses.definition: A small piece of a network message together with information that helps move it.
senses.example: A longer message can travel in many packets.

senses.definition: The worldwide system that connects many networks and lets computers exchange information.
senses.example: I can use the internet to send a message to someone far away.

senses.definition: A large collection of linked pages and other resources that people can open over the internet.
senses.example: The browser helped me find a page on the World Wide Web.

senses.definition: An app that requests and shows web pages.
senses.example: I opened a library website in my browser.

senses.definition: Equipment and software that answers requests for web pages or other information.
senses.example: A web server sent the browser a copy of the page.

senses.definition: A web address that tells a browser how and where to ask for something.
senses.example: The URL leads to a different page on the same site.

senses.definition: A readable name used to identify a place or group of places on a network.
senses.example: Two pages on the site can share a domain name.

senses.definition: A way for devices close enough to each other to join a network using radio signals.
senses.example: I joined the school’s Wi-Fi network.

senses.definition: A device or program that passes packets toward other computer networks.
senses.example: A router can send a message from our home network toward the internet.

senses.definition: A program or service that looks through a list of information to find matches for your question.
senses.example: I asked a search engine for pages about parrots.

senses.definition: An organized set of clues that helps someone or something find information quickly.
senses.example: The search engine checked an index for pages about boats.

senses.definition: An extra copy kept in case you lose the one you use.
senses.example: The backup had my school project after the laptop stopped working.

senses.definition: A device that notices or measures something, such as warmth, pressure, or motion.
senses.example: The sensor told the robot that it had bumped the wall.

senses.definition: An error in software or computer equipment that makes it work differently from how it should.
senses.example: A bug made the game jump back to the start.

senses.definition: To find and fix problems in a program or another system.
senses.example: We stopped to debug the instructions when the score went the wrong way.

senses.definition: In programming, a name used to keep track of a value a program needs.
senses.example: The program keeps the team’s score in a variable.

senses.definition: In programming, a group of steps a program can use as one unit, often by calling it by name.
senses.example: One function draws a star where the player taps.

senses.definition: In a program, instructions that are used only if a particular test has the right result.
senses.example: The game uses a conditional to check whether I reached the end.

senses.definition: In programming, a group of steps that can run repeatedly.
senses.example: A loop tells the game to move the bird a small distance again and again.

senses.definition: Having to do with the two values true and false, or rules that use those values.
senses.example: A Boolean question could ask whether the light is on.

senses.definition: A chart that lists the result of a logic rule for each possible set of true and false choices.
senses.example: The truth table shows when the alarm button should turn on a sign.

senses.definition: Putting things into a useful order or groups, such as from smallest to largest.
senses.example: Sorting the cards made it easier to find the number I wanted.

senses.definition: A way to look in a sorted list by checking the middle and deciding which half to keep looking in.
senses.example: The program uses binary search to find a number in a sorted row.

senses.definition: Details that can help identify a person or tell where to find them.
senses.example: The name of your school can be personal information.

senses.definition: The ability to choose which parts of your life or information other people can see.
senses.example: I asked an adult to help change the game’s privacy setting.

senses.definition: The right to do something or use something that someone else can allow.
senses.example: The app needs permission to use the camera.

senses.definition: A way to sign in that checks two different kinds of proof that you are allowed to use the account.
senses.example: My family turned on two-factor authentication for an account.

senses.definition: A newer form of software that can make changes or fix problems.
senses.example: An update fixed the app that kept closing.

senses.definition: Using digital devices or online services to bully someone, such as by sending cruel or embarrassing messages.
senses.example: I showed a grown-up what had happened so we could report the cyberbullying.

senses.definition: A message designed to get people interested in a product, service, or idea.
senses.example: An advertisement for extra characters appeared during the game.

senses.definition: Something you pay for from inside a game or other app.
senses.example: We check with an adult before making an in-app purchase.

senses.definition: A feature that asks for proof that you are allowed to use a device before it opens.
senses.example: I put on the device lock before I left the tablet on the table.
